The booked kill clause named sonic4_pinned_profile; canonical_pins_agree_with_the_canonical_size_tables is a live non-ignored caller and is the only place pins.rs and the canonical size tables meet. Rewritten to read the pins constants directly (equivalent: under PinnedBaked assembled_len() returned exactly those constants), assertion unchanged, and it executed in the landing run. Byte bar both halves: pins.rs + golden/ diff empty, repin.toml 37 lines touched 0 non-comment, s4.txt/s4_debug.txt md5 unchanged incl. CRC headers. Suite on the merged tree 4156 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, CARGO_EXIT=0, log stamped pwd/HEAD/branch; baseline 4156/0/4, passed unchanged, delta is the two deleted #[ignore]d native_chained_resume proofs (both carried a retirement rationale naming this substrate).

headline: A booking can be right about the rule and wrong about the example it gives for it, and the two go stale on different clocks.
matters: Someone who checks the example finds it does not hold and concludes the whole rule is wrong. That is a worse failure than a note that is simply out of date, and it is invisible to anyone who cites the note instead of running it.
detail: The FIVE-REG row said --bootstrap-canonical cannot place the tree because ojz_effects_editor_act1 is content-derived and has no region. Running the flag: "section 'player_instashield' has no region in the map". Mechanism correct, witness stale. headline: Region sizes are now read by nothing but tests, which clears the last written obstacle in front of the next piece of work.
matters: The region-end conversion wave had one recorded condition to re-check before it could run. The thing it had to be checked against no longer exists, so that wave is now the clean next pick rather than a blocked one.

headline: The assembler everyone shares had been quietly out of date since yesterday morning, and is now current.
matters: Another lane could not build or measure anything until it was rebuilt, and the stale copy predated a change to how the assembler places code - so any number taken from it since yesterday morning could be wrong.

headline: A 'rerun these tests' hint in our tooling turns out to be something nothing can ever contradict, and nearly half of them are incomplete.
matters: When a value drifts, the tool tells a person which tests to re-run. If that list is short, they re-run one, see green, and never look at the two that actually broke - and nothing anywhere would flag it.
detail: repin.toml per-symbol `tests` is consumed only at repin.rs:167-186 to print a rerun hint; no gate, no selection, no effect on generation. 190 of 412 rows omit a consuming test binary (upper bound, name-anywhere grep). Source-confirmed instance: DMA_Overflow_Count declares 1 test, carried by 3 (dma_queue_port:139, dplc_port:471, bg_anim_port:404). Booked REPIN-TESTS-HINT-UNDERLISTED; kept four incoming aeon rows out of the population.

headline: Answered the engine lane's question in a way that saved them a third repeat of a mistake that has cost two landings.
matters: Twice before they discovered too late that new shared names break our tests, after the work was already committed and published. This time it was settled before they built anything.
detail: Port harness does NOT resolve ram symbols by region: every cross-seam symbol is hand-listed in addr_labels as a phase'd one-byte carrier. Enumerated the real population by which tests LOWER the module: dma_queue.emp -> dma_queue_port/dplc_port/bg_anim_port; vblank.emp -> vblank_port/game_loop_port/load_art_port. Corrected their conclusion to full tests lists. Also banked their formulation: a control tells you your model and the world disagree, not which is wrong.

headline: The reference setup nobody could reproduce is now a script that proves it worked.
matters: Getting it wrong made the test suite report about two hundred failures that looked exactly like real damage to the game's bytes. Anyone can now set it up in one command and get a positive signal that it is right, instead of guessing.
detail: scripts/provision-aeon-ref.sh: worktree at the provenance-pinned aeon rev (reachability checked via ls-remote), four reference ROMs verified CRC32+size against the provenance tail, salvador + gen_compression_vectors + emit_sound_blob. Witness is repin --check printing 'pins.rs unchanged'; confirmed twice, second time by executing the script's own printed instruction. Missing inputs present as named [embed.not-found] errors, not as divergence.

headline: Counted the remaining conversion work properly: 50 regions, and I had published two wrong numbers before this one.
matters: It sets the size of the next chunk of the decoupling work, and 47 of the 50 turn out to be simple mechanical changes rather than judgement calls.
detail: Board said ~80; a grep -c said 51 and was published as a correction; the structured parse says 50, the extra hit being repin.toml:39, a syntax-explaining line in the manifest's own header comment. 47 regions own their last byte (pure re-spelling); 3 do not (objdefs->text, dust_spindash->ring_sparkle, player_climb->player_instashield), and objdefs->text is the ambiguous-owner case R6 rules is dropped never attributed. A grep -c counts a spelling, not a population.

headline: Forty five regions now state their own size instead of borrowing the gap to whatever sits next to them.
matters: Those sizes were quietly measuring the space between two things rather than one thing, so any future re-layout would have silently changed them. They now mean what they say, and the game's bytes did not move.
detail: repin.toml end_measures=allotment -> end=section:<name> for 45 of 50. Falsifier held at every repin: 1186 pin fields compared, every change a LENGTH, every length shrank, no BASE moved. Suite 4156/0/2 over 357 binaries on the merged tree, matching the master baseline. Merged c230e37e. Five deliberately not converted: objdefs, dust_spindash, player_climb (last byte belongs to another section), entity_window and children (children_port asserts their end is a shared anchor with the next region, so it is a true allotment by design).

headline: My own setup script was missing a step, and the way it failed made it look like I had broken something else.
matters: A missing file made an unrelated test fail in a way that pointed straight at the work I was holding. I reverted three correct changes chasing it before finding the real cause, and the check I had published as proof of a good setup could not have caught it.

The published witness (repin --check saying pins.rs unchanged) passed with NO listings present: necessary, not sufficient. Root process gap: no baseline run, so every failure was attributable to the parcel by default.

headline: Three of my sixteen decision cards have never been readable on your console - including one ruling that was made on your behalf.
matters: The question about file paths, and the answer someone gave in your place, were both filed correctly and both invisible to you. Nothing in the loop could report that, because the entries matched the written rule and only the console's own reader could disagree.

headline: The engine lane's landing had gone red on eight of my tests; all eight are closed and they can finish.
matters: Their work was stuck behind my tests, so this was the whole suite's critical path. Two of the eight also turned out to be misdiagnosed - by them and by me - and fixing the real causes means the next similar change will not break the same way.
detail: Merged 2a53cbaf, pushed, 357 suites / 4156 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored / 0 skip lines; merged tree byte-identical to the tested tree (empty diff), four files under crates/sigil-cli/tests/, no golden/pins.rs/repin.toml. Group A: aeon's 'latent condition exposed' diagnosis REFUTED by measurement - Cache_Fill_Resume_Col went 0->4 in section.emp and 0->3 in plane_buffer.emp across def98ee5..ec6a4791, introduced by 839d600d; and there were TWO new symbols, not one. Group B: my own 'hand-typed expectation' premise was wrong - the row is deliberately unpinned to avoid circularity; the real cause is Sound_PlaySFX crossing 0x8000, promoting two plain-shape jsr sites from abs.w to abs.l at 2 bytes each.

headline: Correcting myself: the engine lane's parcel did not cause the failures I blamed it for.
matters: A third parcel, weeks of work earlier, introduced the problem and nobody checked in between - so the breakage landed on whoever happened to run the next check. My earlier note and commit message both name the wrong cause; this is the correction, and the real lesson is that the tool always blames whoever is holding it.
detail: Measured: 839d600d (the d-45 canopy fix) adds all 7 references across section.emp and plane_buffer.emp; the clamps parcel's own commits d3b3ab5a and 9ba11115 add ZERO; pickaxe over def98ee5..ec6a4791 names 839d600d alone; it is an ancestor of the clamps merge with 56 commits and no attest between. Three diagnoses were wrong in sequence - aeon's 'latent', mine 'the clamps parcel', and the agent's own git log -S output naming the true commit while its prose said otherwise. Structural cause is aeon's: attest debt accrues silently and is charged to a stranger. Remedy is aeon's: run freeze_preflight.sh at the START of a parcel. headline: I now know which of my own tests lie when the engine's source tree is missing, and which just go quiet.
matters: When the engine tree is absent or half-there, some of my tests blame the wrong thing entirely and most simply vanish from the count without failing. I measured nine different ways of it being missing, because deleting it outright turns out to find almost nothing - it is the half-broken cases that expose the lying tests. One real defect fell out: the suite creates a folder inside the very tree it is checking for, which switches other tests' safety guards off partway through a run, so the same command gives a different answer the second time you run it.
detail: Merged 8a377311 (docs-only, 293-line note, branch apc/absolute-path-classify). Nine scenarios; union 184 NAMES / 61 MISDIRECTS / 397 SILENT / 38 CORRECT-AS-IS over one 398-row reference-dependent population. Buckets are (row, missing-part) pairs, not row properties: all 61 misdirecting rows are silent under some other scenario, so no per-row fix list is derivable from one run. Absent-tree and source-only both give 0 failed exit 0; partial trees find everything (roms-only 29, no-games-data 28, markers 13). Collection intact: 4170 in every scenario against the --list baseline, zero collection deaths. Walk-up finders: none found, established with an LD_PRELOAD interposer after no strace/bpftrace on the box, red-first control 396,785 real-tree touches with AEON_DIR unset vs 0 with it set absent. seam1::emit_sound_blob:729 create_dir_all before any read + contract_closure_corpus root-exists guard = 0 failed -> 53 failed -> 0 failed on one command; mechanism re-derived at source, not taken from the report. Published 322/181/129 retired: does not reproduce under any of literals 110 / call sites 319 / rows-in-file 466 / rows-gated 398.

headline: The suite no longer creates a folder inside the tree it is checking for, and the game's four builds come out byte-for-byte identical.
matters: A test run used to make a directory inside the engine tree before checking the tree was even there, which quietly switched other tests' safety guards off partway through - the same command gave no failures, then 53, then none again. It now checks first and refuses by name. All four builds of the game match the frozen originals exactly, so the engine lane can build on top of this without redoing their own work. All seven places had the same fault, not just the one we found.

detail: crates/sigil-cli/tests/drift_nightly_harness.rs at dd380203. The old assertion was `reader.is_empty() || Path::exists(reader) || reader.starts_with('/')`; the third clause made the second dead so every absolute path passed. Not a blind tightening: requiring existence would redden fresh checkouts and CI, so the unprovable case is NAMED rather than passed - the same remedy applied to the drift report's tree-state fold an hour earlier. Poisoned through the real config on all three branches plus a config-free unit test over all four verdicts. 7/7. The engine lane converged on the same three-valued shape independently.
headline: A check that was supposed to notice a missing file could not tell missing from never-there.
matters: It guarded the link between my nightly check and the engine lane's records. If that record file were moved or deleted, the guard would have kept reporting fine - the one thing it existed to catch. It now distinguishes three situations: the file is there, the file is gone from a folder that exists (which is real breakage and now fails loudly), and there is no folder at all, which happens on a fresh copy of the project and which it now says plainly it cannot judge, instead of quietly calling it fine.

headline: The test suite now tells you how much of itself it skipped instead of just saying it passed.
matters: If the engine tree it compares against is missing, the suite went fully green - passed everything, failed nothing - while quietly not running a large part of itself. Nothing about the result said so. It now states plainly how much it did not measure, and says that a green result does not mean those parts passed. I deliberately did NOT make it refuse to run in that state: that would change things for every lane and it is the open half of a question you already answered once, so it stays yours.

headline: The freeze could build from two versions of the engine and record only one, and nothing would have said so.
matters: The freeze reads which engine version it is working from once, at the start, and then each of its four steps goes and looks again on its own. If that folder changed hands halfway through - and it takes long enough for that to happen - you would get a frozen record that says one version while half its contents came from another. Every later check would still say fine, because those checks read the freeze's own output rather than the folder. It now re-checks between every step and stops if the ground moved.

headline: An assembler nobody could rebuild was about to be written into a permanent record; it is not.
matters: The engine lane was ready to freeze a permanent entry saying which tool built their ROMs. The tool they had used was built from a half-saved copy of my work that no longer exists anywhere, so the entry would have named something nobody could ever reproduce. They stopped and asked instead of freezing, which is the whole reason this went well. I checked what a rebuild could possibly change, said in advance that the ROMs would come out byte-for-byte identical, and wrote that down BEFORE building so it could be proved wrong. It held: all four ROMs identical. Nothing was broken and nothing changed - what we bought is that the record now names a tool anyone can rebuild, and that the one chance to catch a hidden difference was taken rather than skipped. After a freeze it would have been undetectable forever.

headline: A second copy of the project was silently swapping out this one's test programs, and everything looked fine.
matters: The engine lane's safety check went red with 38 problems. Only 2 were real. The other 36 came from test programs left behind by a second copy of the project someone made four days ago and then deleted. The nasty part is not the leftovers - it is that while both copies existed, the build tool could not tell them apart and quietly ran the WRONG one, which passed, because the code was the same. Nothing was detectable. It only turned into a failure when someone deleted the other copy, days later, in a different part of the work, with nothing connecting the two events. I cleared 26 GB of these and proved the failures were gone. The rule we already had - do not let two copies share one build folder - was written down as a tidiness rule; it is actually a correctness rule, and the automated setup already gets it right. The hand-made copies were the problem.
detail: Chain 190 attest 4137/38; 36 were orphans, 2 aeon's real collision_data_port break. Cause: cargo's unit hash is checkout-independent, so two git worktrees of one repo write the same deps/<name>-<hash> and overwrite each other, baking their own CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR. Proven from aeon's own suite-1788092685.log Running lines (cargo ran orphan hashes 2fd3176/616b732/30dbc34/e9c9f90/fcce4d9, never ran ef6422c/06c0a28) and by the rebuild landing on identical hashes correctly baked. Deleted 594 files / 402 executables / 26 GB from three dead worktrees (opt-sweep, pair-delete-percell, pair-showcase); 421 were debug-side, invisible to a --release attest. Post-clean: 0 'No such file or directory', all three named fixture tests pass. Sweep gap closed: .claude/worktrees and sibling .sigil-* checkouts carry 0. Banked f2e9bb06.

headline: This morning's safety change switched off the project's automatic checks, and we only noticed by accident.
matters: Earlier today I made the test suite refuse to run when it cannot find the game engine it compares against, instead of quietly passing while skipping that work. That was the right change and it is still in. What I did not check was the one place that runs the tests automatically on every push - GitHub's servers, which have no copy of the engine. They had been told 'the engine is at this made-up address', which used to mean 'there is none'. The new rule reads a made-up address as a mistake rather than an absence, so those runs started failing this morning. Fixed by telling that setup the truth instead: there is no engine here, this is a deliberately partial run, and here is how much of itself it did not measure. The uncomfortable part is how it surfaced. I was not looking at those automated runs at all. I mentioned in passing that a code-style check was complaining on my machine, and chasing that one remark is what turned up a dashboard showing a hundred failed runs in a row, going back days - so that check had been broken before today's change and nobody in this lane had looked. It is clean again now too. The lesson I am taking is that this lane had a whole automated opinion of its own work that it was not reading.
detail: Branch parcel/d18-followups off master cdd330ff; 5 commits, nothing merged or pushed. CI BREAK (0f9bfbd7): .github/workflows/ci.yml set AEON_DIR=/nonexistent/aeon-not-checked-out-in-ci as an absence sentinel. Under SUITE_PATHS a set-but-wrong checkout variable is a hard error at its own step, so d-18 turned the sentinel into a panic. Reproduced locally before editing: act_descriptor_port 2/2 FAILED with the resolver's own message, and the 'report reference-dependent skips' step then fails on its own zero-skip assertion. Fix: drop the sentinel, set SIGIL_ALLOW_PARTIAL=1. CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED - the opt-in alone IS sufficient with the sentinel still present (set-but-wrong is an Err RETURN at test_support.rs:909, not a panic; aeon_dir routes it to no_named_reference_tree at :1002, which panics only when partial is unset at :1085; verified by running act_descriptor_port in that exact configuration - 2 passed). So removing the sentinel is not what fixes the red; it is right because kept it announces a misconfiguration every run and makes checkout_var_is_set() true, so the sound-write guard takes its passing branch. Unset, only step 3 (refused as a reference tree by design) or step 4 can answer, so the partial path is reached whatever the runner's filesystem holds. All four CI steps run locally with the workflow's own command lines, reporter extracted verbatim from the file: test exit 0 (4198 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, 367 result lines, 397 'skip: ' lines), reporter exit 0 with its zero-branch proven to still fire on an empty capture, clippy -D warnings exit 0, crate-graph guard exit 0. NOT verified on a GitHub runner - that is the owner's follow-up. CLIPPY (e4a5d24d): the 3 findings first reported were only what clippy reaches before aborting per target; enumerated in one pass at warn level the population is 21. 19 taken as suggested, all behaviour-identical. 2 silenced with the reason written down: harness_root.rs's own the_compile_time_manifest_dir_is_only_ever_displayed gate refuses any line naming BUILT_FROM outside a {...} capture, so clippy's useless_format advice compiles, passes clippy and FAILS that gate - made the change, watched the gate catch it, put it back under #[allow]. THE TWO ORIGINAL DEBTS: 444cf295 + e63d2b6d name SIGIL_ALLOW_PARTIAL in landing-run.sh's help and remove it from the landing child with env -u (the -h hard-coded line bound was already fixed on master; 98 -> 118 lines rendered, tail intact). 72e74c64 closes the d-18 bypass: no file under crates/*/tests may read or in-process mutate a reference-tree variable, sanctioned readers identified BY LOCATION so there is no allowlist to hand-edit. Two real test sites found (both in reference_tree_named_write.rs, neither resolving a tree but both second opinions of a precondition the guard owns) now route through a new published test_support::checkout_var_is_set that seam2::require_named_reference_tree itself calls. The gate scans itself, needs no reference tree, and buckets no-reference by the nightly lane's derived rule so SOURCE_GATES was NOT extended (audit: SOURCE_GATES=46 scanned=136 source=45 artifact=85 no-reference=6 unclassified=0). Five red-first proofs, each with the mutation shown on disk and restored from a committed baseline.

headline: Three fixes landed together, including a compiler check that used to fire on correct code
matters: The main one: inside the assembler, comparing two different kinds of thing used to quietly answer 'not equal' instead of refusing. That made one safety check fire on perfectly good code and another never fire at all - and the natural way people fix a check that cries wolf is to delete it. It now refuses and names both types, and when one side is the empty value it suggests the likely cause rather than asserting it. Two more landed with it: an enum value passed to a function from another file was being misread as a plain name, and the three loose ends from the morning's safety change, one of which was that our automatic checks on every push had been failing for days and nobody was looking. The game's four ROMs are byte-for-byte identical, so none of this changes what the cartridge contains.
detail: sigil master 6a8b3ecd (pushed, ls-remote verified) onto the engine lane's chain-197 attest 4d9cbcc8. Merged parcel/comptime-compare-refuses, parcel/imported-enum-variant, parcel/d18-followups. Merged-tree suite 4214 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, exit 0, 369 result lines, 0 skip lines under SIGIL_STRICT_GATE=1, log stamped TREE/HEAD/BRANCH and each parcel's own test names confirmed present in it. Four-shape ROM gate PASS, all byte-identical to the chain-197 goldens: s4 719347/F403F461, s4.debug 736354/50545389, demo 96458/30A31D81, demo.debug 101323/51056291. Reference tree provisioned at aeon 8dd28114, witnessed by repin --check 'pins.rs unchanged'. Known and expected: emp_expect_fail 'tri unit fold' fails on the aeon side until they re-purpose that poison - their half of the agreed pair.

headline: My own proof was produced by the wrong compiler, and a number that disagreed with a prediction is what caught it
matters: Checking that the three fixes changed nothing about the game, I used a four-day-old copy of the assembler without noticing - so 'nothing changed' was true of a build that did not contain any of the fixes. Four matching checksums look exactly the same either way. What gave it away was one count coming out right when it was supposed to come out wrong: a case we knew the fix breaks was passing. The tool that sets up these checks quietly uses whichever assembler was last built in the main folder rather than the one you are testing, which means it can hand back a clean result from the wrong program and nothing about it looks wrong. I redid the measurement properly and it passed for real. Worth fixing in the tool, not just remembering.
detail: scripts/provision-aeon-ref.sh:149 defaults SIGIL_BIN to $SIGIL_ROOT/target/release/sigil - whatever was last built in the main tree (here cdd330ff, pre-merge). A second run of mine used .sigil-ref-target/release/sigil at c230e37e, from 2026-08-29. Tell: emp_expect_fail reported 51/51 where the merged compiler must give 50/51. Re-run with SIGIL_BUILD pinned to the merged binary and the log headed by its --version self-report; the poison then failed as predicted with the new [eq.cross-type] diagnostic, and the four-shape compare passed independently of the build's own CRC line.

headline: The nightly drift watch has now watched something for the first time, and it turned out to have been unable to explain itself.
matters: It had never once written a record in its life. The first real run showed it throwing away the very evidence it exists to produce - including filing its findings under the wrong version of the engine, which would have quietly attributed a real result to the wrong day's work. Fixed, and waiting behind the freeze work.
detail: Hand run authorized via the hub under the standing delegation; the persistent timer stays the owner's own call and was not touched. Ledger ~/.local/state/sigil-ref-drift/observations.jsonl created, 1 row, state NOTHING MEASURED, exit 2. Three suppressions fixed on fix/drift-observer-keeps-its-evidence: provision-aeon-ref.sh reused an existing reference worktree without checking its revision (recorded aeon_rev 73b07a4f against a tree at ddaef90c, 123 commits behind); ./build.sh ran with output to /dev/null under set -e; record_unmeasured omitted --record-reader so the ledger's first row blames a setting that was present. What held: the mtime guard refused to measure copied goldens as a fresh build, its first real exercise. sigil-ref-drift.timer confirmed not installed, so every invocation to date has been a hand run.

headline: Unblocked the engine lane's freeze, which had stopped on three checks in my half of the work.
matters: Two new names the editor now produces had to be taught to the test harness. The third was a four-byte growth nobody had explained; it is now traced to one specific table row rather than left as a plausible story, so the running ledger of where every byte went stays honest.
detail: Branch parcel/item5-cross-seam-composition at 70007a16, pushed and ls-remote verified; landing run GREEN, 4230 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, 371 suites, 0 skip lines, CARGO_EXIT 0, against .aeon-ref-198 at aeon 73b07a4f. EditorRaster_/EditorCycle_OJZ_Act1_ojz_sec3_shimmer wired through repin.toml, pins.rs (from the resolve) and act_descriptor_port. DEBUG_ASSEMBLED_LEN 0xA7F34 -> 0xA7F38: Debug_BandDemoHotkey's .raster_table 8 B -> 12 B, one dc.l row, the next symbol being the first to carry the +4. Also corrected the frozen entry's file-delta decomposition, which double-counted org-anchor-absorbed content. Engine lane owns the merge, four-shape rebuild and re-freeze; the seven golden pairs are the control on the harness-only claim.

headline: The assembler refuses a typo the old one happily builds, and that refusal is now protected from being helpfully undone.
matters: Leaving a bracket unclosed is a real mistake people make; the old assembler builds it anyway and the bug shows up later as behaviour. We stop it at build time. The catch is that this looks like us being incomplete, so someone could 'fix' it back in good faith - there is now a test that goes red and explains why if they try.
detail: crates/sigil-frontend-as/tests/as_unbalanced_bracket.rs at master 70d0f108. `addq.b #2,obRoutine(a0` refused with 'trailing tokens in operand'; controls (closed form, bare nop) assemble in the same run. The first probe reported every case refused including the control, for lack of a cpu/phase preamble - identical messages across subject and control were the tell, and both controls are in the committed file for that reason. Red-first proved with the mutation shown to have landed. Closes AS-COMPAT-UNBALANCED-PAREN-LANDMINE; first measured answer for the new SIGIL-AS-REPLACEMENT project.

headline: Timed a full cartridge build: 1.7 seconds. The engine's build script still advertises 1.15.
matters: This is the number any comparison against the old assembler will be built on, so it is worth having measured rather than remembered. The advertised figure is about half again too fast; corrected before anyone quotes it.
detail: 1.70 / 1.70 / 1.73 s over three runs, median 1.71, producing 719,440-byte s4.bin with sigil 343580a9 via `sigil build --aeon . --native`. aeon's build.sh header books 1.15 s in prose; correction relayed to that lane, whose file it is. Same prose-asserts-what-nothing-executes class as the PROSE-BOUND-SWEEP row.

headline: The nightly drift watch can now report a clean night. Until today it was structurally incapable of one.
matters: It was told to check the game built four ways and only two were ever built - and one unchecked shape spoils the verdict however good the rest look. So its best possible result was 'I could not tell', forever. Nobody investigates a clean result they have never once seen.
detail: provision-aeon-ref.sh gains REF_BUILD_DEMO=1 (opt-in: a landing run needs the demo reference ROMs left as the frozen goldens, the drift job needs them built, and a copied golden cannot exhibit drift). nightly_ref_drift.sh sets it. Proven by run 4: all four shapes measured, no 'shape was not built', state moved NOTHING MEASURED -> UNVERIFIED (exit 3). drift_report.py's ranking was correct and untouched. Remaining blocker is the separate record-coordinate row. First attempt at the proof silently ran the OLD provisioner - the job executes the script from its own detached worktree at origin/master, never the working tree - caught by the absent REF_BUILD_DEMO log line, killed, pushed, re-run.

headline: The watch independently rebuilt all four cartridge shapes and got the frozen bytes exactly, without being asked to check.
matters: The engine lane needed to know a change of mine had not moved a single byte. This reproduced their answer from a different working copy, a different engine revision and a different compiler, with its own comparison switched off - so it could have disagreed and did not.
detail: 4/4 identical against chain 198's frozen entry: demo 30a31d81/96458, demo_debug 51056291/101323, s4 df76de71/719440, s4_debug 0d6d1175/736454. Built at aeon 2986456c (six docs-only commits past the frozen 73b07a4f) with sigil 4b0a17b4, golden control derived as not-applicable so nothing was comparing. Different enumeration parameters from the engine lane's own rebuild, which is what makes it corroboration rather than echo.

headline: The document every session reads at startup was costing more to read than it should. Moved the finished history out, kept every rule.
matters: Six long write-ups of problems already solved were being re-read at the start of every session. They are now one click away instead of in the way, and nothing that still governs the work was cut - the rules they contained were rewritten short and point back at the history.
detail: docs/OVERSEER.md 107,555 -> 91,672 B, 8,328 under the 100,000 B bound. Six closed dated sections moved verbatim to docs/OVERSEER-LOG.md with original line spans recorded. Live rules preserved in a new 'Rules banked from closed findings' section. Split proven lossless: all 1,270 non-blank pre-split lines present in head+log, 0 missing. Line count 1,259 vs the ~900 guide is reported not cut, per the protocol's report-the-residual clause.

headline: Fixed a startup instruction that pointed at two folders which no longer exist - and caught it pointing somewhere worse.
matters: Anyone starting fresh was told to pick the engine reference build from a list of two names, both long deleted, while the one actually in use went unnamed. It now works out which folder qualifies rather than naming any. My first version of that would have sent them to your own working copy, which is the one place it must never touch.
detail: docs/OVERSEER.md at 7d173796. Derives from the definition - a worktree of aeon whose HEAD is the provenance tip's aeon_rev - with two exclusions found by RUNNING the command as written: the aeon main checkout (at the tip whenever the owner has not moved) and .claude/worktrees agent trees. Multiple hits stay correct; the disambiguator is CRC32+size on all four shapes, since an in-flight tree mid-rebuild sits at the right revision with 3 of 4. Third rot of this paragraph: SHA, then name-list, now derived.

headline: Went to start a task, checked whether the problem it described was real, and it was not. Then found two more like it.
matters: My own to-do list had three items stating a general problem from a single sighting, and all three were wrong when tested - two of them made wrong by my own work later the same day. The list is what the coordinating session plans from, so a wrong item there quietly becomes somebody's ordering. Checked the rest and removed the numbers that go stale on their own.
detail: Closed AEON-DIR-RULE-COLLIDES (resolver accepts real reference worktrees; it refused a DELETED path, which is correct). Earlier: OVERSEER-HEAD-RESIDUAL claimed under-the-byte-limit while already 746 B over at boot; DRIFT-DECLINES claimed a design flaw where the expectation record simply holds two hand-typed entries. REPIN-TESTS-HINT-UNDERLISTED made count-free - its '412' became 414 when I added two symbols myself. Booked as a standing row and in session memory: a row is a hypothesis, verify its premise before working it, put the command in the row rather than the number. H-9 and H-11 in the coverage note are unaffected - they stand on their own measurements.

headline: A safety note that had already been corrected was still telling people to do the dangerous thing, just below the correction.
matters: The warning about a hard limit in the cartridge layout was fixed this morning, but the fix was written above the old text and the old text still read as current. Anyone scrolling to it got the original advice: it named the wrong direction as safe, and its check reports a fault on every healthy build. Now marked dead, and the measurement is a script that cannot quietly go out of date.
detail: docs/OVERSEER-ROW-HISTORY.md ABSW-CEILING-INVARIANT at 7455d7aa. Re-measured on chain 198's goldens: every CRC changed since the correction was written and no margin moved - s4 max abs.w 0x7FC6 slack 58 B one-sided, s4.debug 0x7FE6 slack 26 B straddling at 0x82EE. Boundary addresses validated against the listings (Sound_PlaySFX, Raster_Install, Raster_GetChannelBand) so the opcode scan found real transfer sites. Derivation landed as docs/superpowers/probes/absw_ceiling.py - fourth attempt at this measurement and the first that fails to run rather than going stale.

headline: Cut ten process items off my list on your instruction, and the paired-freeze work is no longer holding anyone up.
matters: You asked us to drop what is slowing things down without a good reason. Most of what I had queued was about our own record-keeping rather than the game. Gone. What I kept is the handful that affect whether the output is right.
detail: Dropped: PROSE-BOUND-SWEEP, NAME-MOVER-CHECKLIST, TEST-COUNT-RECONCILER-IS-APPROXIMATE, MY-OWN-ROWS-ASSERT-FROM-ONE-OBSERVATION, SOURCE-GATES-RUN-LIST, ATTEST-RECORDS-REACHABILITY, FREEZE-THE-LISTINGS, PIN-CHAIN-ONE-INSTRUMENT, AB-CART-IDENTITY-SIZE-ONLY, CLOSURE-DEPINFO. Decouple holes dropped: H-7, H-8, H-9(b), H-11 (subject was the paired freeze). Kept H-4, H-9(a), H-10, H-5, H-1's straddle assertion. Flagged as a real dependency rather than polish: the drift observer is now the only net and cannot attribute anything until aeon seeds its expectation record.

headline: My own safety check caught my own comment, and the fix kept the check rather than loosening it.
matters: A check exists so the nightly watcher can never be wired into anything that blocks a build - that is what makes it safe to leave running unattended. A comment of mine mentioned the watcher by name and the check cannot tell a mention from real wiring, so it fired. The easy fix was to add my file to its exemption list; that would have made the check blind to real wiring in a shared file forever, so I removed the mention instead.
detail: Chain 199 attest red on no_landing_path_invokes_the_drift_job; fixed at ddea6956, full suite GREEN 4232/0/2, 372 suites, 0 skip lines, clean tree, and the formerly-red test appears in its own green log. The guard's header already recorded catching drift_report.py's docstring on its first run and chose name-matching deliberately. Also landed the drift record's append cadence in DRIFT_RECORD_SEAM.md (d4f08038) - one entry per landing, a requirement the engine lane accepted first, with the caveat that a record built only from freezes holds only agreements so entry count is never coverage.

headline: The engine has moved on past the copy we test against, which is what we wanted, and I checked it breaks nothing.
matters: Ending the paired freeze means the engine can land on its own. It has - twelve commits and a byte change since our frozen copy. The thing worth checking was whether that makes our nightly checker start crying wolf, because a nightly alarm nobody can silence is exactly the kind of drag you asked us to cut. It does not.
detail: Chain 200 (aeon 8876459e) verified reachable, 12 commits past pin 73b07a4f, byte-moving, unpaired. Three of the nightly lane's 46 gates read frozen baselines; the lane runs at aeon TIP and its own log shows exit 0 at 05:19:28 today, and the baselines are maintained against tip, so H-5's frozen-corpus concern is future-state not tonight. My first attempt measured a BARE worktree and got 22 'generated file absent' failures I nearly reported as real - my own documented trap. Also found d-18 already landed: aeon_dir() no longer falls back to the owner's live tree, so that section's stated justification is stale though its rule stands.

headline: Proved the nightly watcher can actually catch a problem, rather than assuming it. It can - and its blind spot is not in the code.
matters: Ending the paired freeze made this watcher the only thing standing between a bad build and nobody noticing, so 'it probably works' was not good enough. Fed it a deliberately wrong result: it reported the fault, named which shape was wrong, left the healthy one alone, and exited with the failure code. What it cannot do is say 'all clear', and that is because the list of expected answers is nearly empty - not because anything is broken.
detail: Through the real CLI against a stand-in reader at the job's own coordinates: true CRCs -> QUIET exit 0; one nibble perturbed -> DRIFT exit 1, drift-same-pair on the perturbed shape, quiet on the untouched one in the same run. Corrects my own H-10 fact 3, which named the two verdicts that DO fire as the unreachable ones: the unreachable half is cases 1 and 2, the only ones advancing N. drift_report.py selftest already gates the state machine (all four cases pass), so no new gate; what was missing was a record entry.

headline: Item 5 is closed on the engine lane's frozen record rather than on my account of it.
matters: The editor-authored cycle and its colour variants reach the cartridge, and the harness work I owed for it is certified by the frozen entry rather than by my say-so.
detail: Chain 199 entry name=item5-cross-seam-composition, aeon_rev 73b07a4f unchanged from 198, note records the goldens byte-identical and the entry existing to abandon 198 because the fix for its red moved no bytes. Freeze commit baa9bb03 verified an ancestor of origin/master. Suite green 4232/0/2 at ddea6956 after the one guard red.

headline: The tool that tells you which tests to re-run after a pin moves was quietly naming too few of them.
matters: When an address shifts, the tool prints the tests you should re-run. That list was typed by hand and nothing checked it, so it could be wrong forever without anyone finding out - and 176 of 386 entries were. It now works the list out from what actually reads each address, so it cannot be short.
detail: repin.rs derives the hint from which crates/*/tests/*.rs reference the constant; repin.toml's `tests` field marked unread. Proof on a real pin move: Map_TestObj declares objdef_port, five binaries read MAP_TEST_OBJ, doctoring the pin emitted all five; pins.rs restored and verified. Over-reports by design (a comment mention counts) which is the safe direction for a do-not-forget hint. An empty sweep is reported, not printed as an empty hint, because the walk assumes a fixed root. Suite GREEN 4232/0/2 at 22b1a19f, clean tree.

headline: Made the two file-path conventions in the engine source tolerable from both sides, so neither repo has to wait for the other.
matters: The engine spells embedded-file paths two ways and we had a hardcoded exception for the one module that differs. I had claimed the fix needed both repos to change in one go; that was wrong, and a tolerant middle step means each side can move on its own schedule. The assembler now accepts either spelling, says which files still use the old one, and the count of those is the progress meter.
detail: Landed 5d7e1511, suite GREEN 4232/0/2, clean tree. resolve_sandbox_path tries project-root-relative first, falls back to module-relative, warns [embed.module-relative] per SITE naming file and line. engine.math exception retired; the closure hands every module its own directory from the manifest. Byte-neutral, measured: pins.rs unchanged, native_full_rom 3/3. Fires on exactly 2 sites in each of 7 shapes. First run was RED - the new lint id was unadjudicated - so it is now in CORPUS_LINTS plus two site-pinned CORPUS_OPEN_FINDINGS rows whose kill condition is step 3. Also generalised the register's matcher, which was coupled to the one lint's wording and so blamed the new row.

headline: The nightly drift watch is switched on. It runs at 07:17 and one command turns it off.
matters: Since the engine and the assembler stopped certifying together, this watch is the only thing that would notice a cartridge quietly changing. It had never run. It now runs nightly, and today it was proved to catch a deliberately planted fault rather than assumed to. To stop it: systemctl --user disable --now sigil-ref-drift.timer
detail: d-21 supersedes d-20; ruled `enable` by the hub in the owner's place on his 20:25:12Z go, banked empyrean 0963b04. sigil-ref-drift.timer enabled+active, first firing Thu 2026-09-03 07:17 EDT, OnCalendar 07:17, Persistent=true, no contention with aeon-effects 04:17 or sigil-source-gates 05:17. d-20's option text said 05:47 and was wrong; corrected in d-21. I declined this twice today on the silence-is-not-consent argument and both rulings were withdrawn; what changed is that the card reached his list and he gave a go to decide that list.

headline: Correction: I said the engine had not landed something, using a record that had stopped tracking the engine that morning.
matters: Separating the two projects means our frozen record no longer follows the engine's releases - which is the point of the separation. I forgot that and read our record as if it still did, so I reported a landing missing when it was simply somewhere I had stopped looking. The engine's chain 201 is real.
detail: Claimed no chain 201 existed from sigil's provenance chain (tip 200, aeon_rev 8876459e). Verified after the hub's correction: aeon b81e5daa 'merge: chain 201 - the OJZ canopy drifts' is reachable on their origin/master, and their tip cb0e5eb1 is 7 commits past my chain's last aeon_rev. The instrument stopped measuring the subject the day the coupling was cut, by my own work, and answered about my tree instead of saying it could not see. My other two observations hold and are aeon's: no item-3 lane-log entry, and tools/drift_record.jsonl still two lines.

headline: The engine lane landed its half of the path fix. Mine has to wait, for a reason the plan had not accounted for.
matters: We deliberately test against a frozen copy of the engine, and that copy still uses the old spelling. So removing our support for it would break our own checks even though the engine itself has moved on. The plan assumed one engine tree; separating the projects gave us a second one that does not move by design.
detail: aeon bbe74e4f landed step 2, verified reachable, all four shapes byte-identical. Meter: embed.module-relative = 0 at aeon origin/master, = 2 against .aeon-ref-198 (aeon 73b07a4f), which is what our byte gates build; provenance pins aeon_rev 8876459e. The fallback fires only after root-relative fails, so it is load-bearing for the pinned corpus and step 3 is gated on the pin advancing past bbe74e4f - a decouple sequencing decision, raised to the hub. Also answered aeon's drift-record question: no backfill even flagged, because the lookup matches on revisions and never reads an origin field, so a flagged reconstruction would still produce a real QUIET and advance N.

headline: The shared assembler everyone reaches by default was built from a branch I had deleted, and had stopped being able to build the engine.
matters: Anyone using the default path got a hard failure on the engine's current source, while the engine lane's own builds passed because they point at a different copy - so it was invisible to them and fatal to everyone else. Rebuilt. The engine lane found it and correctly refused to fix it in my checkout.
detail: target/release/sigil was stamped sigil 2eb47a92, branch trial/drift-plus-item5 - MY DELETED trial-merge branch, not an ancestor of master; the object survives only because git has not collected it. It failed aeon master with [call.live-clobbered] (D1c) GONE firing Parallax_Update @ Decode_Factor_B, reproduced here at aeon bbe74e4f. Rebuilt from master 0a58f2ec: md5 6c2378ae8a657e26684d4019a7d976d7, builds aeon master exit 0, zero D1c and zero embed errors, crc=a573d280 len=719648 matching aeon's reported chain figure. CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULE: my OVERSEER bullet says a relink overwrites the shared binary in place and destroys a freeze's assembler. The unrecorded half is that it can stamp it with a revision that later CEASES TO EXIST, so the artifact's provenance is unreproducible rather than merely old. My first reproduction attempt also built ../aeon, which is the owner's live checkout at 73b07a4f, not master.

headline: Found that 76 of our 387 routines claim to destroy more registers than they actually touch.
matters: When a routine says it destroys a register, every caller has to assume the worst and work around it. One routine claims ten registers and touches one. That is real optimisation lost, and nothing currently notices - we check the opposite mistake but not this one. Measuring it was the job; fixing it is a campaign because it shifts a baseline the engine's build checks against.
detail: declared_clobbers minus closure.effective over all seven shipped shapes: 76/387 on sonic4 plain, 62 on debug. Sample-validated: Air_CeilingBump declares clobbers(d0-d7/a1-a2), writes only d0, calls one proc adding nothing. Gap-ledger row updated at 996350d6 from 'method banked' to measured, with why it is not the small lint it reads as: ~76 warn-tier firings need adjudication, and the tightening moves D1c firings which aeon's contract gate builds against. Measured with a ContractReport.nodes field added then reverted - unused pub fields are what that ledger catches.

headline: Our byte-for-byte checks currently have no engine copy they can run against, and two of our own commits did it.
matters: We test against a deliberately frozen copy of the engine. Sixteen minutes apart we froze that copy at one day's engine, and updated a contract list to expect the NEXT day's. So pointing at the frozen copy fails the contract check, and pointing anywhere else fails the pairing check. Nothing is wrong in either project - the two records describe different days - but until one moves, the byte checks cannot run and any red they produce is not a regression.
detail: sigil master vs the pinned aeon 8876459e: NEW [call.live-clobbered] firing Parallax_Update @ Decode_Factor_B :: d2 (got 1, want 0) - the exact mirror of the GONE firing aeon saw from their stale binary, same proc and register, opposite direction, which is what identifies the single cause. 3fabac20 (15:29, D1c per-game axis for band drift) expects aeon chain 201+; c27335d6 (15:45, freeze chain 200) pins aeon 8876459e, before it. Also fixed en route: provision-aeon-ref.sh crashed with a bare traceback reading [entry.strict.goldens] on a frozen-but-unattested tip; both readers now prefer [entry.targets.*] and refuse by name. Held uncommitted - not landing script changes into a lane whose gates cannot run.

headline: Tried to advance our frozen copy of the engine. The safeguard refused, for a good reason, and the way round writes something permanent - so I stopped.
matters: A refreeze is not allowed to build on a previous one that was never fully checked; that rule exists because two earlier ones smuggled a stale value through. Checking the previous one first is impossible, because it is the exact copy that cannot build. The tool's designed answer is to record a deliberate failure and then supersede it - which is a permanent line in a record that cannot be edited, so it is not mine to write without being asked.
detail: Provisioned aeon 4f5ad5a1 clean (both shapes built, listings emitted, shared binary untouched at 6c2378ae - aurora anchors on that md5). Capture completed all seven shapes; append refused: tip tails-jump-gate #200 carries no strict run while #173 does, so the strict-attestation ratchet is in force. Discarded via the tool's own option 2 and PROVED: seven goldens, seven size tables and pins.rs restored, journal removed, s4.bin back to 864ad7e9/719460, git status clean but for the uncommitted provisioner fix. Options put to the hub: deliberate red attest then supersede (recommended), --retired-strict-gates (weakens a rule that caught real bugs), or leave the pin - which post-cut may mean never, since only sigil advances the chain now.

headline: Advancing our engine copy nine versions brought fourteen failures. Three groups fixed; the last two are measured and left for a clearer hour.
matters: Every one of the fourteen is a check correctly noticing the engine moved - none is a defect in either project. I fixed the three that were unambiguous. The two left need care rather than speed: one is a block of memory offsets our test copies by hand from the engine and which is now exactly 64 bytes out of date. Editing those at quarter to one to make a gate go green is how a wrong green gets made.
detail: Closed: the embed transition retired with its lint and register rows (the register's own trigger demanded it), the port harness's embed base repointed to the root, and player_common's two new cross-seam names wired (Collision_GetType already pinned - repin caught my duplicate; CrossoverTable new at 0x700AC/0x7096C). Left: parallax_port's hand-copied ram.emp offsets, stale by BAND_DRIFT_BYTES 4 x MAX_PARALLAX_BANDS 16 = 64 (its own comment says 20 x 16 = 320 where the tree now needs 24 x 16 = 384); proper fix is to derive them from ram.emp per the harness's own section-4 pattern rather than re-copying. And generated_pins_match_the_hand_typed_baseline needs its per-parcel term for the new corpus.

headline: Two of the three remaining failures are fixed and pushed. One of them was our test copying the engine's memory layout by hand, so I stopped it copying.
matters: When the engine adds a feature that makes each background band a little bigger, every address below it shifts. Our test had those addresses typed out by hand, so it was describing last week's engine and failing for a reason that was nobody's fault in the engine. It now reads the addresses out of the engine's own build output, which cannot be out of date. The earlier note said the drift was 64 bytes; it was 128 - the same four-bytes-per-band cost lands in two different places, and counting one of them looks like a complete answer.

headline: Our own test-run summary could say 'these tests did not run' directly underneath the list of tests that had just failed.

headline: The test that was supposed to clear the way for separating the two projects can now be passed by something that does not work.
matters: Separating the assembler's tests from the live engine depends on a nightly watch taking over the checking. The condition written down for that was 'prove one nightly observation lands'. But not one of those entries can ever reach a conclusion, because the answers it compares against are in a file that has two stale lines in it. The condition was passable while the thing was broken, which is the more general lesson: 'prove it runs' and 'prove it can produce the answer it exists for' are different tests, and the first is the one people write down because it is the one that is easy to check.

headline: First look at making Sigil assemble the public Sonic 2 disassembly. One real defect fixed, and the biggest problem is that our error messages never say where.
matters: Running Sigil on the disassembly from outside its folder produced 59,122 errors, starting with five complaints about files that are plainly there - it was looking for them in whatever folder you happened to be standing in. One line; fixed and shipped; now 237 either way. The bigger finding is that not one of those 237 messages tells you a filename or a line number, in a 91,000-line file. AS - the thing we would be replacing - does tell you. On the single dimension of saying where the problem is, we are currently behind it. That is also blocking my own next pass, because without locations I cannot walk from an error count back to the code that caused it.
detail: docs/superpowers/notes/2026-09-03-as-replacement-first-pass.md. Fix: sigil 4e22e536 (CLI called assemble(&str) not assemble_root(&Path), leaving include_root unset), red-first, suite GREEN 4233/0/2. Corpus s2disasm e45ebf3, 332 files/130,025 lines, s2.asm 91,276. Nameless labels settled as d-22 for the @as_compat surface: 1875 defs / 1764 refs, control 2040 rts tree-wide. Locations: Diagnostic carries primary: Span and SourceMap::location exists, but sigil-frontend-as builds no SourceMap and stamps SourceId(0) everywhere - a real parcel, not a one-liner. Five hypotheses refuted by minimal case (# modulo, endm closing rept, set/equ/:= on plain names, dotted locals under a global label, rept from equ/backward-label arithmetic). Still broken: nameless labels, rept from same-line and forward labels (the latter: did not converge within 16 passes), backward org, digit-leading labels (s2.sounddriver.asm:159 1upPlaying:), unquoted macro args with spaces. The 30 malformed-number diagnostics remain UNEXPLAINED after two wrong mechanisms; corpus-wide string-stripped scan finds only 4 occurrences.

headline: Our error messages now say which file and which line, the way AS does - and the first thing they told us is that the whole Sonic 2 disassembly has been assembling as the wrong processor.
matters: Last night's headline was that not one of our 237 error messages named a file or a line, in a 91,000-line program spread over 332 files, while the assembler we want to replace prints both. That is fixed: all 237 now say where, and there are still exactly 237 - a diagnostics change that quietly moved the count would have been hiding something. The locations paid for themselves within the same run. Those 237 errors turn out to come from only 128 distinct places, and three lines account for 112 of them. They also overturned my own explanation from last night. The 30 errors I could not account for are nothing to do with macros: line 55 of the disassembly says CPU 68000 in capitals, we only recognise it in lower case, and our default when nobody tells us is the Z80 - on which a dollar sign means 'here' rather than 'a hex number follows'. So we have been assembling a Mega Drive game as if it were a Z80 program, and every $1A fell apart. Capital letters are now the single largest thing standing between us and this disassembly: 115 of the 237.
detail: Merged c03bc7e5, pushed at master 7538fced (verified with git ls-remote, not the tracking ref). Landing run on the final committed tree: 4237 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, 374 suites, zero skip lines, cargo exit 0, reconciles 4237 + 0 new; log stamped pwd/HEAD/branch/clean, and all three --expect-test names present. Byte witness positive not absent: s4 crc=14ee2440 full=719700, s4.debug crc=142294b3 full=737683, the provenance tip's own values. Mechanism: SrcLine carries the SourceId of the file it was read from (per line, not per assembler, which is what makes a macro report the file its body was written in rather than the call site); directive_include registers each spliced file; failing pass returns Failure { diags, sources }; CLI renders file(line). A span belonging to no registered file prints bare rather than being pinned to line 1. Four red-first proofs, each quoting the mutation from disk before the red run with the predicted failure stated first. Case finding verified here independently of the agent's runtime repro by reading eval.rs:1956 (matches "cpu" lower case only), lexer.rs:75 ($ is Tok::Dollar under Cpu::Z80) and lib.rs:29 (initial_cpu defaults to Z80) - different enumeration parameter, so corroboration rather than echo. Note docs/superpowers/notes/2026-09-03-as-source-map.md.

headline: Our landing check has been printing a confident GREEN while one of the things it is documented to check was never being run at all.
matters: Every parcel here ends with a landing run that prints a verdict block - tree, revision, counts, RESULT GREEN. The written standard for that run lists four requirements, and one of them is the code linter passing with warnings treated as errors. The script does not run the linter. Not skipped, not degraded - the word does not appear in it. So the block reads as complete while a listed requirement is simply unmeasured, which is worse than a missing check, because the verdict actively tells you everything passed. When I ran the linter by hand it failed on master, and had been failing since a parcel earlier the same day. Both errors were harmless - an unused keyword and a line of documentation that began with a plus sign, which the linter reads as a bullet point - and that is rather the point: nothing was going to surface them, so the next real one would have sat there just as long.
detail: scripts/landing-run.sh: grep for clippy returns zero hits; the bar in docs/OVERSEER.md lists `clippy -D warnings exit 0` alongside the count, the zero-skip requirement and cargo exit 0, and describes the wrapper as carrying every requirement inside one command span and REFUSING rather than degrading when one is missing. Errors fixed at 526ae99e: unused_mut at sigil-frontend-emp/src/eval/sandbox.rs:129 (from fb649ae9, same day) and doc_list_item_without_indentation at sigil-frontend-emp/tests/cond_branch_witnesses.rs:56 (from df49808a, 2026-09-02, a wrapped `instruction_address + 2` quote). --all-targets is load-bearing: the first appears in a lib build, the second only when test targets are checked. cargo clippy --release --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings now exits 0 with zero crate-level errors. NOT yet wired into the wrapper - that is the actual fix and is booked, because hand-running it is the same maintenance model that failed here.

headline: Split the document every fresh session reads first back under its size limit - and then my own rulings from this morning put it back over the same day, which is the finding.
matters: That file is the first thing any new session here reads, so its length is a tax paid on every restart. It was a third over. Eleven closed episodes moved out to the archive beside it, each one sitting under a rule that stayed put - the rule survives, the war story moves. Nothing was lost: I checked that twice by different methods, and both checks were built so they had to be able to fail, because a broken check and a clean result look identical. It came in under the size limit at 98,202 bytes, and then the rulings I banked this morning took it back to 100,657. That is not a mistake to fix by trimming - it is the shape of the problem. A document that has to carry every live ruling will cross any fixed line on any working day, and choosing between a bigger allowance and a different structure is yours.
detail: Merged docs/overseer-bound-split at 8b585910; pushed master 3f6713eb. OVERSEER.md 1,423/104,225 -> 1,340/98,202 -> 1,370/100,657 after the day's rulings; OVERSEER-LOG.md 5,627 -> 5,834 lines, append-only verified (numstat 0 deletions both appends). Losslessness proved twice over different parameters - agent's sorted-unique set difference, and here an exact per-line grep -qxF of all 85 removed non-blank lines against the log plus byte-level numstat (96 out, 170 in, 0 log deletions); exactly 5 removed lines absent, all 4 rewrites, each enumerated with before/after. Both runs carried a control that had to print and did; my first pass had two false MISSING results from needles spanning line breaks and three from lines beginning '-' being parsed as grep options, fixed with --. Rewrite #1 was a defect fix: the landing-lane row read 'ripples past pins.rs into pins.rs', source and destination identical, garbled by an earlier edit; facts re-verified here (repin.rs:89 root.join("src/pins.rs"), :192 sole write, mixed_dac_rom.rs and engine.inc untracked, repin_pins.rs a currency gate). Agent's method finding banked as a standing rule: a losslessness proof certifies no text was lost and nothing about whether surviving text still parses - a sentence whose antecedent moved passes every line check.

headline: The public Sonic 2 disassembly stops being assembled as the wrong kind of machine - it had been treated as a Z80 program, and capital letters were why.
matters: The whole point of this project is that the community's disassembly should build with our assembler instead of the old one. It was failing with 237 errors, and 115 of them came down to capital letters: the file says CPU 68000 in capitals and we only recognised it in lower case. Our fallback was the Z80, a different processor entirely - where a dollar sign means 'here' rather than 'a hex number follows'. So every address in a Mega Drive game was being read as the wrong thing. Now it reads as a 68000, and for the first time that path actually runs: the file count we get through went from 4 of 332 to 7, and the error count rose from 237 to a much larger number, which is the good outcome and was written down as the expected one before the work started. Those are not new breakages; they are the first sight of work that was always there and hidden behind the first wall. The guard that mattered: the game's own cartridge is unchanged, byte for byte, all four builds - because three of the engine's own files go through this same code path, so getting it wrong would have quietly changed the shipping game.
detail: master 15bb1ef2 (merge), parcel 5bbfb2c0 + note aedb77b8. One file: crates/sigil-frontend-as/src/eval.rs, +345/-53, one fold_kw helper applied at every site that DECIDES keyword-hood; Tok::Ident and all define/resolve paths untouched. Byte gate: control build at 9abb7dc6 reproduced 14ee2440/142294b3/0c456778/2e603d53, post-fold rebuild (ROMs deleted first, four separate build.sh invocations) reproduced all four identically; freshness witnessed by mtimes 03:12-03:18 against the 03:04 fold commit. Landing run on the merged tree: 4246 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, 374 suites, 0 skip lines, exit 0, reference .aeon-as-fold @ 4f5ad5a1 clean; clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0 run separately since the wrapper does not carry it. +9 tests (eval.rs 127->136, reconciled). Three red-first mutations, each quoted from disk and restored from the committed baseline; mutation B (fold at the token) reddens both symbol guards, 21 tests. s2disasm 237 -> 85335 counts / 8486 distinct sites, zero of the 129 before-diagnostics surviving. Agent corrected the dispatch brief: five folded sites are unreachable from dispatch, including the colon-label EQU form s2.constants.asm actually writes, so the controller's seven-row enumeration would have left the headline EQU cases broken. Register names deliberately not folded (all uppercase D0/A0/SR in the corpus are inside comments; a label named A0 would misclassify). Booked open: z80undoc and AS's CPU-name set, bchg/exg/roxl, eleven AS directives, the macro-body nesting gap.

headline: The assembler now refuses to guess which processor a program is for, instead of quietly picking the wrong one - and the check that was supposed to prove the refusal worked turned out to prove nothing, which the agent caught itself.
matters: This is the other half of last night's finding. Capital letters explained why the Sonic 2 disassembly was read as the wrong machine, but that only got fixed because that file happens to say which processor it wants. Anything that says nothing was still silently assembled as a Z80 - a completely different chip - and nobody would be told. Now it stops and says so, printing the exact line to add. The delicate part was scope: one of the engine's own files deliberately says nothing, because the file that pulls it in has already said it. Refusing per-file would have broken your build on a file that is correct. So the refusal is per program, not per file, and there is a test standing on exactly that. The honest headline, though, is the check that did not check anything: the agent's own test for the error appearing in the right order passed whether or not the feature was there, because the example it used had only one message to order. It noticed by deliberately breaking the feature and seeing the test stay green, then rebuilt the test on an example that could actually fail and re-proved everything after it. Byte guard held again - all four builds of the game identical.
detail: master 4d9809e4 (merge), parcel f3056dc3 + gate fix 6365bf3e + derive 724cadd5 + note 5498feb1; ruling-name fix 4e9ecce3. Options::initial_cpu -> Option<Cpu>, None default (setting it IS declaring); AsmState::cpu_declared one-way latch deliberately outside the save/restore snapshot so restore is not a declaration; two detection points, Asm::emit (single call site of builder.emit_data) and end-of-one_pass_with_defer for a byteless unit; PROVISIONAL_CPU=Z80 retained so the only behavioural change is the refusal. 88 files, 644/-170, of which 83 are mechanical initial_cpu: Cpu::X -> Some(Cpu::X) (verified: every changed line outside the three core files mentions initial_cpu). Refusal fired on no aeon file; aeon tree not edited. Red-first: mutation A (cpu_declared:true) 5 red, B (per-file scope) 1 red - the hazard guard alone, C (drop the diagnostic hoist) GREEN = vacuous, fixed in its own commit by re-basing the assertion on FOO equ $10 with a diags.len()>=2 precondition, C re-run red, everything after re-established. Enumeration: 485 initial_cpu sites classified by owning literal (LowerOptions 339 untouched, AsOptions 112, Options 34); exactly ONE caller declared nothing - sigil-cli/src/main.rs:98 Options::default(), the shipped CLI, left inheriting the refusal deliberately. No existing test relied on the silent default (suite green on the type change before any gate), so the default was serving no in-tree caller and only mis-serving outside users. headline: The assembler used to read the processor's name and throw away the number - so a program for a completely different chip assembled cleanly as a Sonic one.
matters: This is the same silent-wrong-answer fault we closed twice this morning, found behind a third door, and it was the one nobody was looking for. The visible complaint was that we rejected the Sonic 2 sound driver. One line above that, any processor name written as a number was being discarded and replaced with the Mega Drive's, so two unrelated chips assembled clean and said nothing. Fixing the visible half alone would have shipped the dangerous half untouched.
detail: Landed at master 253468e5 (merge of parcel/as-cpu-variant-spellings, six commits, pushed and verified against the remote). directive_cpu's name extraction read Some(Tok::Int(_)) => "68000": the VALUE was discarded, so `cpu 6502` and `cpu 68020` both resolved to M68000 and assembled clean at exit 0. The `68008` arm that the dispatch brief cited as the precedent for the accept-only-what-we-encode rule was therefore dead code - 68008 never reached it. Spellings now live in one table (CPU_SPELLINGS in sigil-frontend-as/src/lib.rs) which the refusal text enumerates back to the reader, so the diagnostic cannot advertise a spelling the directive will not take. A spelling earns a row only when it names an instruction set sigil encodes: same ISA different packaging (68008), or a superset whose extras refuse by name (z80undoc). 68020/z180/gbz80/6502 stay refused. Soundness measurement behind accepting z80undoc: every undocumented form refuses and emits nothing, including the index-register halves the driver uses 12 times - but that refusal reads 'unresolved symbol ixl', not 'unimplemented register', so a source defining a symbol of that name would get a silent wrong encoding. Nothing in the corpus does; making it unconditional means touching a function shared with the 68000 path, so it is booked, not done. Corpus: diagnostics 85,335 -> 89,120 (the driver's real gaps become visible for the first time), but s2.asm's distinct unresolved symbols fell 302 -> 207 - 95 symbols, the whole sound-ID block, became resolvable. Verification on the merged tree: landing run GREEN, 4259 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, 376 suites, zero skip lines, reconciles; all six new tests present in the run's own log; clippy --release --all-targets -D warnings exit 0, zero Rust warnings; all four aeon shapes rebuilt from the merged binary in .aeon-default-cpu (a tree the agent never touched) and byte-identical - s4 14ee2440/719700, s4.debug 142294b3/737683, demo 0c456778/96474, demo.debug 2e603d53/101339 - with build mtimes as the freshness witness, since matching CRCs on a byte-neutral parcel cannot themselves prove the build ran. Two of the agent's own gates were found weaker than claimed and rebuilt: one derived its expectations from the same table it was auditing (a table cannot audit itself), one matched text belonging to a neighbouring diagnostic. Corrections to my own records: the boot doc's bar saying a landing emits exactly one 'ratchet:' line is stale - 28 chain entries carry strict attestations, so zero is the correct post-attestation state, which that same paragraph's disarm sentence predicts. Also banked earlier at a8e88c66: the owner's cut-the-ceremony ruling, which had reached this lane through mail only.

headline: All seventeen Sonic 2 zones were sharing one identity, and nothing complained about it - the level art pointer table was computed against a single zone's number for every zone.
matters: This one is worth more than it looks, because no count could ever have found it. The source builds a symbol name by pasting a number into it, one per zone. We were throwing away the pasted part, so every zone defined the SAME name and the last one silently won. There was no error message before the fix and none after - it simply produced wrong addresses. It is the fourth silent-wrong-answer fault closed on this project today and the only one that was invisible to every measurement we had.
detail: Landed at master a8cbb45d (merge of parcel/as-macro-variadic-shift; the branch name predates the determination and does not describe the content - shift itself is scope-blocked). AS symbol-name composition implemented: a {expr} group outside a string literal and outside a comment evaluates and pastes into the surrounding identifier, any position, several per name, defining side too, string->characters and integer->decimal; inert inside quotes and after a semicolon; an unresolvable group is a hard error, never a pasted prefix. Also \{expr} now folds where a string is BOUND rather than where it is read, matching asl. The silent defect: s2.constants.asm:375 'zone_id_{cur_zone_str} = zoneID' truncated at the brace, so all 17 zoneID invocations ($00-$10) defined the collapsed name zone_id_ with last-write-wins, and s2.asm:88545's '!org LevelArtPointers+zone_id_{cur_zone_str}*12' folded against one zone's id for every zone. Verified here independently against master's own binary: a two-definition probe collapses to a single symbol. MY DISPATCH HYPOTHESIS WAS REFUTED, which is the delivery's best feature: I briefed that shift and the org failure were one root cause because both fired exactly 32,351 times. Two probes separated them - the shift walk with a brace-free org gives zero org errors, one brace group with no recursion gives exactly one. shift supplies the multiplier (a self-call consuming nothing recurses to the expansion cap, re-emitting both lines per iteration), the brace group supplies the error; identical counts were co-location times runaway. A third cause the brief never anticipated then surfaced and gates the rest: sigil scopes a macro body's .-local set VARIABLES per expansion, where asl scopes those to the caller while scoping .-LABELS per expansion (verified both ways with asl -L). Sigil is right for labels, wrong for set variables; all 32,385 remaining brace failures are the single name {.cur_zone_str}. Numbers: corpus diagnostics 89,120 -> 121,505, distinct unresolved symbols FLAT at 207 in s2.asm and 298 across all files. The rise is one precise unresolved-composed-name error per runaway iteration replacing one that named a symptom, every other bucket byte-identical. The flat symbol count is the honest ceiling on what name composition can reach while the scope rule is unfixed - reported rather than dressed up. Verification on the merged tree: landing run GREEN 4265 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, 376 suites, zero skip lines, reconciles as 4259+6; all six new tests present exactly once in the run's own log (the four other new fns are implementation helpers); clippy --release --all-targets -D warnings exit 0; all four aeon shapes rebuilt from the merged binary and byte-identical, mtimes 05:34 -> 06:53-06:59 as the freshness witness. Red-first: three mutations each shown applied from disk and restored from a committed baseline, and no test expectation came from running the new code - every value is quoted from an asl -L listing. Scope-blocked with sizing: shift (35,167 diagnostics; needs macro-body substitution to become lazy, ~10 evaluator sites that ship aeon bytes), .-local set scoping (gates 32,385; aeon-byte-risky), label + {INTLABEL} (5,353), then eval (3,417), Z80 $-as-PC (752 + 749 cascade), strlen on a function param (996), irpc (370), charset (82). Process note for my own conduct: my first landing run died because I put it inside the harness background task that watched it - the run and the watcher were one process group, and reclaiming the watcher killed the work. Relaunched under setsid with the waiter separate. This lane's own doc already says do not watch work with a harness background task; it did not say do not LAUNCH it as one.

headline: One bad line in the Sonic 2 disassembly was being reported sixty-four times over, and the fix cut our complaint count from 121,505 to 22,328 without hiding a thing.
matters: The directive that walks a macro's argument list was missing, so one macro called itself forever until it hit our expansion cap - and every genuine error inside that macro got re-printed on every lap. What we were looking at was not 121,505 problems. It was about 22,000 problems shouted repeatedly, and the noise made the remainder unreadable. The part worth trusting is the negative result: no new kind of error appeared, no kind got worse, and the set of names we cannot resolve is identical before and after, both directions. A fall that size normally means something was uncovered, and here the honest answer is that nothing was - the win is that what remains is now one complaint per site. Separately: this crate is in the game engine's own build path, so the parcel could have moved shipped game bytes, and all four ROMs rebuilt bit-for-bit identical.
detail: Landed at master 6ba5fb21 (merge of parcel/as-macro-shift, three commits, pushed and verified against the remote by ls-remote). RECOVERY, not fresh work: the implementing agent died with the 14:07Z account restart; its two commits survived on a harness auto-branch (worktree-agent-a232a0d2ce289451d) and its 243-line note was UNCOMMITTED in that worktree. No ref named parcel/as-shift-directive ever existed here - that name is the note's own header, which is where the hub's report picked it up. Preserved as parcel/as-macro-shift before anything else. Implementation: an expansion pushes a MacroFrame and executes the RAW body, substituting .ATTRIBUTE/ALLARGS/parameters where a line's text is consumed (exec_one, dispatch_head, def_function, capture_macro, capture_struct, parse_struct_field); parameters empty-fill behind the shift rather than re-windowing; loop and capture constructs deliberately stay eager, which the fourth parcel's sizing had wrongly listed as lazy sites - six sites plus a loop-capture rule, not ten. Verification, all re-checked here rather than taken from the note: strict landing run 376 suites 4273 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, exit 0, zero skip: and zero ratchet: lines, log stamped with pwd/HEAD/branch and carrying 47 mentions of the parcel's own subject; the three 'panicked at' lines are #[should_panic] tests printing their panic, not failures; clippy --all-targets 0 errors (the wrapper still does not run clippy - LANDING-RUN-NO-CLIPPY stands); all four aeon shapes DELETED then rebuilt from the branch binary at .aeon-as-fold (detached at provenance tip aeon_rev 4f5ad5a1), CRC32+size matching the frozen tip on every one (s4 14ee2440/719700, s4.debug 142294b3/737683, demo 0c456778/96474, demo.debug 2e603d53/101339), mtimes moved so the match is a positive witness rather than an absence; one of the eight red-first proofs re-run as a sample, the re-windowing mutation redding EXACTLY the one test the note predicted (192 passed / 1 failed) with the tree left clean of it. Pre-merge bar satisfied by derivation rather than assumption: master was an ancestor and the merged tree hash equals the branch tree hash (a0d1deb6), so the strict run on the branch IS the merged-tree run. Suite delta +8 corroborates the eight-test deliverable against the prior 4265 figure, though that baseline is a quoted prior measurement and not one re-derived here. Count corroboration is coarse by design - the boot doc's grep tripwire undercounts macro-bodied tests. Also fixed in the same session: the boot doc claimed a fixed ratchet: count for the third time; it now derives the expected count from whether any chain entry records a strict run. OPEN, and it is the one task the dead agent never reached: asl upper-cases the argument values it rebuilds ALLARGS from after a shift while sigil preserves the text as written, and sigil's symbol names are case-sensitive - whether that can reach a composed symbol name or emitted data is unanswered, booked as AS-SHIFT-ALLARGS-CASE. Two divergences ratified as deliberate: AS's emptied-parameter placeholder bytes are not replicated (the corpus only exercises the never-bound case), and ARGCOUNT plus keyword-argument interactions are booked rather than guessed.
